nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
nodes.criteria: Judge only the requested transformation, using both support observations. Return yes when the DVD is visibly white rather than black and retains its identity as a DVD. program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

This raises a target-correspondence/identity ambiguity, not evidence that the requested color change made no progress. Tighten the binding to track the specific DVD from the source through the edit, and make the decision assess that same object’s visible color and DVD identity rather than treating generic disc appearance or support observations as independent proof. Preserve the rubric’s partial and unresolved outcomes when color progress or identity is uncertain. The five identical high-confidence yes traces suggest a systematic criterion/binding issue, not a transport or dependency failure; the reference label alone does not establish which visual criterion failed.

The edited image shows a white disc at the DVD’s approximate location, but its correspondence and DVD identity are uncertain; the other object also appears changed. Do not treat generic disc appearance as proof of identity or of complete fulfillment. Keep the node focused on its identity role, while ensuring the overall decision separately evaluates the requested color change on the tracked target and preserves partial or unresolved outcomes when progress or correspondence is uncertain. The repeated high-confidence passes indicate a systematic binding/criterion problem, not a transport or dependency failure. Do not infer the correct label from the reference alone.

The edit shows a white disc near the source DVD’s location, but the source object’s printed square appearance is no longer evident, while the separate black object to the right also appears altered into a disc. Treat this as correspondence/identity uncertainty, not proof that no change occurred or that the request is complete; leave fulfillment and partial/unresolved classification to the rubric and appropriate checks.
